What happens next: Natalie steps away from the family to kiss him, teasing him about his halftime retirement. Adrian thanks him for playing, still smarting at the margin. Julian stays beside Claire rather than volunteering congratulations. Let the encounter breathe.
Force nothing. Let the moment breathe, and answer only what the Move does.
answer:
Natalie stepped away from the group before Claire finished saying something about the equipment van.

“There he is.”

She came straight over, slipped a hand around the back of his neck and kissed him. Her bag slid down her shoulder; she caught it with her elbow without moving away.

“Enjoy your retirement?” she asked. “I was watching you sit there thinking, *God, he’s taking this remarkably well. Such dignity in his later years.*”

Her thumb brushed his neck.

“Seventy-one points, then two quarters of watching Stephen demand applause. Difficult working conditions.”

Behind her, Daniel rested a hand on the handle of Claire’s rolling case.

“Should’ve charged admission by the basket.”

“We’d have had complaints,” Claire said.

“From Adrian.”

Adrian gave his father a flat look, but the corner of his mouth moved.

He stood a few feet from the rear of the family’s car, his foundation jersey replaced by a dark shirt. He shifted his keys into his other hand as he approached.

“Thanks for coming out. Seriously.” He held out his hand. “The Henderson girls are going home talking about twenty-three threes. They’ll remember tonight.”

A beat passed.

“I might’ve preferred they remember a slightly closer game.”

Natalie glanced back. “You invited the Warriors.”

“I remember the invitation, Nat.”

“You put their name on the posters.”

“Thank you. Very helpful.”

Her smile softened, but she didn’t leave Roopesh’s side.

Adrian looked back towards him. “Hell of a shooting night.”

The compliment was plain. So was the effort it cost him to leave it there.

Claire checked that Daniel had the case, then tucked her phone into her handbag.

“And thank you for staying for the photographs afterward. We got everyone through much faster than I expected.”

Julian remained beside her, one shoulder turned towards the car. He was holding the foundation album while she searched for her keys; when she glanced at him, he passed it over without needing to be asked.

“Front seat?” he asked.

“Yes, please. Not under the case.”

He opened the passenger door and laid it flat inside. He offered no congratulations, busying himself with making room for Claire’s bag.

Natalie watched her mother for a moment, then turned back. The white twenty-one shifted beneath the strap on her shoulder as she adjusted it.

“I yelled so loudly Dad asked whether Stanford offered a quieter major.”

“Still a fair question,” Daniel said.

She laughed, then caught the edge of Roopesh’s sleeve between two fingers.

“Anyway. I believe I booked some time with you after the match.” Her voice dropped, warm with the unfinished joke from before tipoff. “Unless your retirement calendar’s already full.”

answer:
Steph threw both arms up before the roar had finished climbing.

“No. No, that’s ridiculous.”

He was laughing too hard to sound remotely disapproving. Along the Warriors bench, Melton stepped away from the scorer’s table with his hands on his head; Horford caught his elbow and steered him back.

“We still have to check in.”

**31–21, Golden State. 5:43 left in the first.**

Seventeen points for Roopesh. Two more threes, and a block that had turned an anticipated dunk into a highlight going the other way.

Natalie was on her feet.

“That’s my boyfriend!”

Daniel glanced up at her, eyebrows raised.

“Yes,” she said, still clapping. “I know whose jersey I’m wearing.”

Claire’s applause was more restrained. Down on the floor, Adrian motioned for the inbound quickly, before the building could enjoy a replay together.

Julian had landed safely, but his expression had closed. He looked once towards the overhead screen, then away.

“Again,” he told Booker, holding out a hand. “Give it back.”

Booker accepted the inbound and kept the ball.

“Get a stop first? Or we running the offence?”

“Run it,” Bell called, stepping to the edge of his coaching box. “Nikola up top. Adrian—behind!”

Jokić met Booker above the arc. Julian came towards the ball with his palm still open, and Jokić pointed him through to the right corner instead.

Julian’s jaw shifted. He went.

“Don’t chase the last play!” Kerr called from the opposite sideline.

Steph settled into his defensive stance against Booker, his grin finally narrowing into concentration.

“Man,” he said, just loud enough for the nearby Warriors, “we are absolutely not getting a relaxing game now.”

Booker handed off to Jokić and curled around him. Porziņģis came forward to contain the exchange; Draymond edged towards the middle, calling out Durant’s position on the opposite wing.

Adrian took two measured steps towards the perimeter.

Then he planted and cut behind Gui.

“Backdoor!” Draymond barked.

Jokić had the ball at his chest, his body still angled towards Booker. His eyes moved to the lane.

At the scorer’s table, Melton and Horford remained standing. No whistle, no substitutions—and Select had stopped waiting for the crowd to quiet down.

plan: What happens next: Natalie accepts his answer without inventing hurt. Claire gathers her beside Adrian and Julian for the photograph. Afterward, Natalie returns to his warm-up, initiating familiar affection and teasing rather than another explanation.
answer:
“Okay. Back in a minute.”

Natalie brushed her fingers over his shoulder before heading towards the camera.

Claire immediately caught her by the elbow.

“Here, darling. Beside your brother.”

“I’ve heard rumours he’s here.”

“Nat.”

Adrian hooked an arm around his sister’s shoulders. “She’s been like this all afternoon.”

“And yet you put me in promotional material.”

The photographer laughed and asked Daniel to turn slightly towards the light. Julian shifted to make room for him, then took the place on Natalie’s other side that Claire indicated. Behind them, the foundation display showed its first scholarship class: six children holding certificates much too large for their hands.

“Can we get the logo clear?” Claire asked.

Natalie pulled her hair over one shoulder, uncovering the lettering across her jersey. Adrian straightened his mother’s lanyard where it had twisted.

For a moment, his attention left the camera.

“Did the Hendersons get downstairs?”

“Yes,” Claire said. “Both girls. Front row.”

“Good.”

The photographer brought them back with a raised hand.

“Right here, everybody. One, two—”

The first flash caught Natalie laughing because Daniel had quietly told Adrian to stop standing like a nightclub bouncer. The second got everyone looking forward. Claire requested one more, checked the little screen, then requested the first one again.

“Mum, that isn’t how photographs work,” Natalie said.

“Just smile.”

Julian grinned. “You know she’ll get it.”

“I know exactly where Adrian gets it.”

This time the photographer lowered his camera decisively. “We’ve got it.”

Natalie slipped out from under her brother’s arm.

“Thank you,” Adrian said, quieter.

She squeezed his hand once. “Go raise a disgusting amount of money.”

By the time she reached Roopesh, a ball had bounced loose near the tunnel. A court attendant scooped it up before it reached the warm-up space; farther out, Curry’s latest shot snapped through the net.

Natalie crouched beside Roopesh, balancing with one hand on the floor.

“Four photographs. Apparently my left eye wasn’t sufficiently committed to charity.”

She leaned in and kissed his cheek, unhurried despite the activity around them. Her bracelet slid towards her hand as she settled beside him, knees bent, careful to leave his ankles room.

“Also, Mum has discovered the burst setting. Christmas is going to be unbearable.”

From the court, Steph called, “Twenty minutes!”

Natalie lifted a hand in acknowledgment, then glanced at Roopesh’s shoes.

“I’m not interrupting the sacred ankle proceedings. I’m merely attending.”

Her shoulder rested lightly against his.

“Very exclusive event. Terrible seating.”
